value.body: HRIS executives look after the software an organisation uses for HR: employee records, leave, attendance, onboarding and appraisal workflows. They work in company HR teams or at HR software vendors and implementation partners. The work mixes data upkeep, report building and helping employees and HR colleagues use the system.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA (HR), BCA, or any graduate with strong Excel skills

items.label: Common starting titles
items.value: HRIS executive, HRMS associate, HR systems analyst

items.label: B.B.A. enrolment (all specialisations)
items.note: HR is one of several BBA specialisations; no separate HR count
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 11 (programme-wise enrolment, all modes, actual responses)

items.label: B.C.A. enrolment
items.note: Another common entry degree for HR-systems work
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 11 (programme-wise enrolment, all modes, actual responses)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Entry is often through HR operations roles, then moving towards system work, or through HR software vendors that hire freshers for implementation and support. Comfort with data, Excel and learning new software is the main filter.

value.title: At a glance
items: Sits between HR and IT, so learning both sides helps.
Common next steps: HRIS analyst, HR analytics, or HR software implementation consultant.
Data accuracy and privacy carry real responsibility in this role.
